  Q.1   If 𝑃𝑐= [𝑥𝑐, 𝑦𝑐, 𝑧𝑐]𝑇locates the Center of mass of a rigid body
         relative to {𝐴}. Then the Parallel-axis Theorem, relates the
         inertia tensor in a frame {𝐶} with origin at the center of mass
         to the inertia tensor with respect to another arbitrarily translated
        reference frame {𝐴} as,

      A) ᴬ𝐼𝑧𝑧 = ᶜ𝐼𝑧𝑧 − 𝑚(𝑥𝑐² + 𝑦𝑐²)

       B) ᴬ𝐼𝑧𝑧 = ᶜ𝐼𝑧𝑧 + 𝑚(𝑥𝑐² + 𝑦𝑐²)

       C) ᴬ𝐼𝑧𝑧 = ᶜ𝐼𝑧𝑧 × 𝑚(𝑥𝑐² + 𝑦𝑐²)

      D) ᴬ𝐼𝑧𝑧 = ᶜ𝐼𝑧𝑧 / 𝑚(𝑥𝑐² + 𝑦𝑐²)

       Answer: B
        Refer to Lecture 11: Acceleration of a Rigid Body Slide 17

Q.3  In Euler's equation 𝑁 = ᶜ𝐼𝜔̇ + 𝜔 × ᶜ𝐼𝜔, what does the term
     ᶜ𝐼𝜔 physically represent?

     A) Linear momentum of the body

     B) Angular momentum of the body

     C) Gravitational torque on the body

     D) Total kinetic energy of the body

     Answer: B
      Refer to Lecture 12: Newton – Euler’s Equation Slide 9


Q.4  Using Newton's equation 𝐹 = 𝑚𝑣̇𝑐, if a link has mass m = 4
     kg and its center-of-mass linear acceleration is 𝑣̇𝑐 = (3, 0, 4)
      m/s², what is the magnitude of the force F acting at the center
      of mass?

     A) 12 N

     B) 16 N

     C) 20 N

     D) 28 N

     Answer: C
     Using 𝐹 = 𝑚𝑣̇𝑐: F = (4×3, 4×0, 4×4) = (12, 0, 16) N
     Magnitude = √(12² + 0² + 16²) = √(144+256) = √400 = 20 N

Q.8  In the expression for the kinetic energy of the i-th link, 𝑘𝑖 =
                                                 𝑐𝑖                          𝑇·   𝐼𝑖 · ⁱ𝜔𝑖, what do the two terms    ½𝑚𝑖· 𝑣𝑐𝑖𝑇· 𝑣𝐶𝑖 + ½ · ⁱ𝜔𝑖
      physically represent?

     A) Both terms represent kinetic energy due to linear velocity,
     computed in different reference frames

     B) The first term is KE due to linear velocity of the link's center
      of mass; the second term is KE due to angular velocity of the
      link

     C) The first term is potential energy due to height; the second
     term is kinetic energy due to rotation

     D) The  first term represents  actuator  torque; the second
      represents joint friction

     Answer: B
      Refer to Lecture 14: Lagrangian Formulation of Manipulator
     Dynamics Slide 8
